summary.headline: Southborough library trustees reviewed state certification standards, prepared for an upcoming state construction grant round, and discussed drafting a patron behavior policy.
summary.summary: The Southborough Library Board of Trustees met to review operating finances, state certification compliance, and upcoming capital grant opportunities. Library Director Ryan Donovan confirmed the library satisfies state expenditure requirements, avoiding decertification risks. The trustees reviewed recent facility repairs, closing time enforcement, and plans to draft a formal patron code of conduct and trespass policy. Preparations were also initiated for the Massachusetts Public Library Construction Program grant round, including an updated building condition assessment and a public survey.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board opened the meeting, reviewed and approved the amended minutes of the October 5 meeting, and concluded routine proceedings.
key_details: Meeting was called to order at 11:03 a.m.
October 5 minutes approved as amended with typographical corrections.
Meeting adjourned at 12:03 p.m.

topics.title: State materials expenditure requirements and library certification
topics.summary: Trustees discussed state financial standards governing library materials spending and confirmed the town is not in jeopardy of losing state certification.
key_details: State reporting excludes office supplies from materials expenditure calculations, counting only educational and library collections.
While the state baseline target is 16 percent of the budget, Southborough's minimum requirement is reduced to 14.4 percent due to extended evening and Saturday hours.
The director reported there is no danger of state decertification this fiscal year assuming the town budget is approved.

topics.title: Library facility and infrastructure updates
topics.summary: The director provided updates on completed and upcoming facility work, including lighting, book drop walkways, and municipal phone upgrades.
key_details: Automatic timer switches in the teen room were replaced with manual switches.
Concrete walkway replacement around the book drops was completed for $4,100 paid from state aid, below the $5,000 authorized cap.
Town-wide phone system migration is underway; the library will remain open Friday despite Town House office closures.
The municipal facilities department took custody of the library's new exterior sign to obtain specialized masonry screws for installation.

topics.title: Teak bench replacement and Choate Fund application
topics.summary: Trustees discussed replacing a damaged outdoor teak bench and agreed to postpone purchasing until spring.
key_details: The damaged teak bench was previously removed following winter weather damage.
Trustees chose to defer acquiring a new bench until spring to prevent immediate exposure to winter weather.
The director plans to apply for grant funding from the town's Choate Fund when applications open in April.
topics.outcome: Decision to wait until spring to seek grant funding for a replacement bench.

topics.title: Patron behavior, closing enforcement, and trespass policy
topics.summary: The director and trustees discussed an Election Day incident, police inquiries regarding trespass notices, and the enforcement of library operating hours.
key_details: Police were called after a patron printed and left materials at public terminals and removed local history items from designated areas.
The patron did not commit a crime and was not trespassed, but police inquired about library trespass authority.
The library currently lacks a formal trespass policy.
The director shared a complaint relayed from a private tutor regarding 5:00 p.m. closing enforcement and furniture placement.
Trustees supported staff closing procedures, emphasizing the necessity of clearing the building promptly at closing.
topics.outcome: Board agreed on the need to draft a formal policy governing patron behavior and trespassing.

topics.title: Programs and operations update
topics.summary: The director reported on game cataloging, upcoming book sales, regional library initiatives, and end-of-year meeting scheduling.
key_details: Staff indexed and relocated Nintendo Switch games behind the front circulation desk to prevent missing items.
The Friends of the Library will hold another book sale on December 5.
Southborough will participate in the regional One Book One Burrough initiative with Marlborough, Westborough, and Northborough in the spring.
Trustees discussed moving their December meeting to 4:00 p.m. to coincide with the annual staff holiday potluck.

topics.title: Library budget and salary expense report
topics.summary: The director provided an update on operating expenses, staff salary lines, and preliminary municipal budget reviews.
key_details: Salary overages are diminishing as the director covers vacant desk shifts and overtime costs decline.
Outstanding staff longevity payments were processed in recent payrolls.
The preliminary FY28 library budget was submitted to the Select Board without initial concerns raised.

topics.title: State construction grant preparations and building assessment
topics.summary: The director briefed trustees on preparations for the Massachusetts Public Library Construction Program grant round opening next year.
key_details: The Massachusetts Public Library Construction Program plans to open a grant application round early next year.
The library must procure an updated whole-building condition assessment, targeting a cost below the $10,000 procurement threshold.
A targeted community survey focusing on facility needs is being developed to replace earlier open-ended surveys.
topics.outcome: Director authorized to solicit proposals for a building assessment under $10,000.

topics.title: Patron code of conduct drafting timeline
topics.summary: The board outlined next steps for creating a comprehensive patron behavior policy and code of conduct.
key_details: The director will prepare a consolidated patron code of conduct and behavior policy including trespass criteria.
A draft policy will be presented to trustees at the December meeting.
The policy will be reviewed with town legal counsel and police before formal adoption.
topics.outcome: Draft policy scheduled for presentation in December.

Trustees meeting and annual staff holiday potluck
